items.title: upfadapter: Association Setup Response handler drops UP Function Features, so the SMF never learns the UPF can allocate UE IPs
items.body:
## Summary

`pfcp/adapter/adapter.go`'s `HandlePfcpAssociationSetupResponse` records `UPFStatus`, `RecoveryTimeStamp` and `NHeartBeat` from the Association Setup Response, but never records the **UP Function Features** IE. The native handler in `pfcp/handler/handler.go` does.

The two are on mutually exclusive dispatch paths, so with `enableUPFAdapter: true` the SMF permanently believes the UPF supports no optional features — including UEIP.

## Why it matters

`UPFunctionFeatures` has exactly one assignment in the tree:

```go
// pfcp/handler/handler.go:375
if rsp.UPFunctionFeatures != nil {
    UPFunctionFeatures, err := ies.UnmarshalUserPlaneFunctionFeatures(rsp.UPFunctionFeatures.Payload)
    ...
    upf.UPFunctionFeatures = UPFunctionFeatures
}
```

That block has no counterpart in the adapter handler. Downstream:

```go
// context/upf.go:602
func (upf *UPF) IsUpfSupportUeIpAddrAlloc() bool {
    if upf.UPFunctionFeatures != nil &&
        (upf.UPFunctionFeatures.SupportedFeatures1&UpFunctionFeatures1Ueip) == UpFunctionFeatures1Ueip {

// context/datapath.go:591
if dpNode.UPF.IsUpfSupportUeIpAddrAlloc() {
    ueIpAddr.CHV4 = true          // ask the UPF to allocate
} else {
    ueIpAddr.V4 = true            // use the SMF's own allocation
    ueIpAddr.Ipv4Address = smContext.PDUAddress.Ip.To4()
}
```

So in adapter mode `CHV4` is never set, the UPF is never asked to allocate, and the SMF's local allocator is authoritative — even when the UPF is explicitly configured to allocate. Both handlers contain the `PDUAddress.UpfProvided = true` path that consumes a UPF-allocated address, but in adapter mode nothing can ever cause one to be sent, so that code is unreachable.

## Observed

UPF configured with `enable_ue_ip_alloc: true`, which makes it advertise the UEIP bit (`pfcpiface/messages_conn.go:113`, `pfcpiface/utils.go:31`). SMF running with the adapter:

```
INFO  adapter/adapter.go:215  handle PFCP Association Setup Response with NodeID[10.43.79.49]
```

and the resulting PDR carries the SMF's own address with `CHV4` clear:

```
UEIpAddr:[&{192.168.100.3 <nil> false true false false false ...}]
                          V6=f  V4=t              CHV4=f
```

The same deployment with the native PFCP path sets `CHV4` and the UPF allocates.

## Dispatch paths, for reference

Adapter responses do not go through `pfcp.Dispatch`; they arrive synchronously and are routed by `HandleAdapterPfcpRsp`:

```go
// pfcp/adapter/adapter.go:139
func HandleAdapterPfcpRsp(pfcpMsg message.Message, evtData *udp.PfcpEventData) error {
    switch pfcpMsg.MessageType() {
    case message.MsgTypeAssociationSetupResponse:
        HandlePfcpAssociationSetupResponse(&msg)   // adapter's own, no UPFunctionFeatures
```

Confirmed on `upstream/main`: `pfcp/adapter/adapter.go` has 0 references to `UPFunctionFeatures`; `pfcp/handler/handler.go` has 5.

## Suggested fix

Record the IE in the adapter handler as the native one does. The parse is already factored into `ies.UnmarshalUserPlaneFunctionFeatures`, so it is the same handful of lines.

More generally, the two association-response handlers have drifted, and any feature negotiated at association time will be silently absent in adapter mode. It may be worth extracting the shared post-accept body so the two paths cannot diverge again — the `UpfProvided` block is already duplicated verbatim between them.

## Related

This is the mechanism that makes #621 reachable in practice: because the SMF is forced to be the allocator in adapter mode, the unbounded `(SMF_COUNT-1)*5000` stride described there is what the UE actually receives.

items.title: UE IP allocation walks outside the configured pool after SMF restarts (SMF_COUNT stride is unbounded)
items.body:
## Summary

`IPAllocator.Allocate` offsets every UE address by `(SMF_COUNT-1) * 5000`, where `SMF_COUNT` is a **monotonic counter incremented on every SMF start**. Nothing bounds that offset against the configured pool, so after a handful of restarts the SMF hands out addresses that are outside the subnet the deployment routes — silently, and in one direction only.

On a `/24` pool this breaks on the **second SMF start**.

## The code

`context/db.go` — at startup, the counter is read from Mongo and pushed into the process environment:

```go
smfCount := mongoapi.CommonDBClient.GetUniqueIdentity("smfCount")
logger.DataRepoLog.Infof("unique id - init smfCount %d", smfCount)
os.Setenv("SMF_COUNT", strconv.Itoa(int(smfCount)))
```

`context/ip_allocator.go` — every allocation is strided by it:

```go
smfCountStr := os.Getenv("SMF_COUNT")
if smfCountStr == "" {
    smfCountStr = "1"
}
smfCount, err := strconv.Atoi(smfCountStr)
ip := IPAddrWithOffset(a.ipNetwork.IP, int(offset)+(smfCount-1)*5000)
```

## What we observed

Configured pool `192.168.100.0/24` (`UeSubnet` received correctly — the SMF logs it on every config poll). After 195 cumulative SMF starts:

```
context/db.go:65          unique id - init smfCount 195
context/ip_allocator.go   unique id - offset 2
context/ip_allocator.go   unique id - ip 192.183.49.18
```

The arithmetic closes exactly:

```
192.168.100.0 + 2 + (195-1)*5000  =  192.168.100.0 + 970,002  =  192.183.49.18
```

The UE accepts the address, the PDU session establishes, and **uplink works**. Downlink is dead, because the address matches neither the route nor the NAT rule the deployment installs for the pool:

```
192.168.100.0/24 via <upf-core> dev core
-A POSTROUTING -s 192.168.100.0/24 -o <uplink> -j MASQUERADE
```

Uplink leaves unmasqueraded with an unroutable source, so replies are never generated. Every counter upstream of the UE looks healthy; only `ping` fails.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy with a `/24` UE pool and `enableDBStore: true`.
2. Attach a UE — it gets `192.168.100.x`, and everything works.
3. `kubectl rollout restart deploy/smf` **once**.
4. Re-attach the UE.

The address is now offset by 5000 (`192.168.119.x` for a `192.168.100.0/24` pool), outside the pool. Downlink stops; uplink continues.

## Why we think it is a defect

The stride appears intended to keep multiple SMF instances from allocating overlapping addresses. Two properties break that intent:

1. **The counter measures starts, not live instances.** It is monotonic and never released, so one SMF restarted N times is treated as the Nth concurrent instance. In Kubernetes, restarts are routine.

2. **The offset is unbounded relative to the pool.** A `/24` has 254 usable addresses; a 5000-address stride leaves it immediately, and leaves any pool smaller than a `/19`. There is no check that the result is still inside `a.ipNetwork`, and no error when it is not — the address is handed out and the session comes up.

The failure is silent and asymmetric, which is what makes it expensive to diagnose: the SMF, UPF and UE all report success, and only the return path is missing.

## Possible directions

Any one of these would address it; we have no preference:

- Bound the offset by the pool and fail the allocation loudly when the slice does not fit.
- Reject at startup a `(smfCount, stride, subnet)` combination that cannot fit, rather than at allocation time.
- Derive the per-instance slice from a **lease** that is released when an instance stops, so the value tracks live instances.
- Size the stride from the configured subnet rather than a hard-coded 5000.

## Workaround

Reset the counter and restart:

```
db.getSiblingDB("sdcore_smf").counter.updateOne({_id:"smfCount"}, {$set:{count:1}})
```

This holds only until the next SMF restart.

## Note for anyone debugging this

`SMF_COUNT` is not a deployment variable. It does not appear in the pod spec, `envFrom`, the run script, the image, or `/proc/<pid>/environ` — because the process sets it on itself after exec. `os.Getenv` sees it; the process environment does not show it. That cost us some time.

items.title: The Configuration order causes PFCP Association Request Failure
items.body:
The following configuration order in webconsole causes PFCP Association Setup failure.

- Create a network slice with empty device group
- Create a device group
- Create a subscriber

SMF log:

`2023-11-30T20:55:48.294Z [smf] 2023-11-30T20:55:48Z [ERRO][SMF][PFCP] Handle PFCP Association Setup success Response, DNN mismatch, [internet] is not configured`


Please check the following issue for more details:
https://github.com/omec-project/webconsole/issues/89
